courses.subject: BIOC
courses.title: Biochemistry Orientation
courses.description: Lectures designed to acquaint biochemistry majors with the various specializations available in the field, career exploration procedures, and a wide range of opportunities of special interest to biochemistry students.
courses.prereqText: Biochemistry Specialized Curriculum majors, transfers and first year freshmen only.

courses.subject: BIOC
courses.title: Undergraduate Open Seminar
courses.description: Approved for both letter and S/U grading. May be repeated.

courses.subject: BIOC
courses.title: Individual Topics
courses.description: Laboratory work and/or reading in fields selected in consultation with an appropriate faculty member. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 10 hours.

courses.subject: BIOC
courses.title: Gene Expression & Regulation
courses.description: Provides in-depth and up-to-date coverage of gene expression and regulation. Lectures are centered on the principles of regulating gene expression in eukaryotic cells. The course covers macromolecule structure and function in gene expression; molecular mechanisms of the key gene expression events including transcription, RNA processing, localization and translation. Applications of these principles in medicine and therapeutics such as aging, cancer and drug design are also discussed. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours.

courses.subject: BIOC
courses.title: Physical Biochemistry
courses.description: Physical properties of biological macromolecules, with the emphasis on spectroscopic methods, including UV, visible and FTTR spectroscopies, magnetic resonance techniques as well as X-ray diffraction methods. Same as CHEM 472 and MCB 446. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: It is strongly recommended to take CHEM 440 (section B) prior to this course. MCB 354 or MCB 450 or equivalent background in biochemistry is also recommended.

courses.subject: BIOC
courses.title: Technqs Biochem & Biotech
courses.description: Introduction to modern methods of experimentation with biochemical experimentation. Lectures and labs on the theory and practices underlying various methods and instrumentation. Includes protein purification and quantitative analyses, immunoassays, enzymology, peptide sequencing, lipid analysis, carbohydrate analysis, and bioinformatics. 4 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 232 or CHEM 236, or equivalent; credit in MCB 251 or equivalent, and MCB 354 or MCB 450 or equivalent, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOC
courses.title: Biochemistry Senior Seminar
courses.description: Writing intensive course dealing with the technical literature, current issues, and current advances in Biochemistry. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours. Graduate students may register, but priority will be given to undergraduate students.
courses.prereqText: Completion of the Campus Composition I general education requirement; MCB 354 and BIOC 455, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOC
courses.title: Senior Thesis
courses.description: Limited in general to seniors in biochemistry. BIOC 492 is recommended for all those who plan to do research and graduate study, and it is a prerequisite for graduation with distinction in biochemistry. Each student who desires to do thesis research must receive written permission from a member of the biochemistry faculty. Accordingly, prospective students are encouraged to contact the biochemistry staff in the term prior to registration in this course. Students must present a thesis to receive credit in this course. 1 to 6 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit. May be repeated; enrollment is limited to three semesters.
courses.prereqText: MCB 354 and BIOC 455, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOC
courses.title: Anlys Biochemical Literature
courses.description: Discussions of current research and literature. Required of all graduate students whose major is biochemistry.
courses.prereqText: Second year graduate standing in biochemistry or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOC
courses.title: Individual Topics
courses.description: Designed for students in biochemistry who wish to undertake individual studies of a non-Ph.D. thesis nature under the direction of a faculty member of the department. Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated. (Summer Session, 1 to 8 hours).

courses.subject: BIOC
courses.title: Biochemistry Seminar
courses.description: Students, faculty, and invited speakers present seminars and discussions on current research topics. Required of all Biochemistry Ph.D. students. Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated to a maximum of 12 hours.

courses.subject: BIOC
courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated in the same term or in separate terms.
